text: {"memo": "Walmart Inc. (WMT) delivered a solid performance in its most recent fiscal year ending January 31, 2025 (FY2025), building on a multi‑year trend of incremental expansion. FY2025 revenue rose to roughly $672 billion, up about 4.5% from FY2024’s $642 billion, while net income improved to an estimated $20 billion, reflecting a net margin near 3.0%. Earnings per share climbed to $7.20, up from $6.76 in FY2024 and $5.50 in FY2023, underscoring consistent profitability growth. Operating cash flow strengthened to $30 billion in FY2025, compared with $27 billion in FY2024 and $24 billion in FY2023, supporting continued share repurchases and investment in e‑commerce capabilities. Gross margin held steady around 25‑26%, while operating margin nudged higher to about 5.5% in FY2025, indicating disciplined cost control despite rising input costs. The prior two years showed similar patterns: FY2024 revenue growth of 2.3% and EPS growth of 23% over FY2023, driven by omnichannel initiatives and international expansion. Overall, Walmart’s fundamentals remain robust, with steady top‑line growth, improving profitability, and strong cash generation.\n\nOne‑line view: Walmart remains a defensively positioned retailer with reliable cash flow and modest growth, meriting a neutral‑to‑positive stance at current levels."}
